title: TPS cleared of wrongdoing in deaths
subtitle: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has cleared a Timmins Police officer of any wrongdoing in connection with a fatal shooting at Gillies Lake last winter.
article: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has cleared the Timmins Police Service of any wrongdoing in connection with two unrelated deaths that occurred on a single weekend in February 2018.
Joey Knapaysweet, 21, was shot dead on frozen Gillies Lake on the morning Saturday, Feb. 3, when he lunged at a police officer while armed with a kitchen knife.
There is evidence in the SIU report to suggest Knapaysweet was suicidal and intent on provoking police to kill him.
The officer initially tried using a conducted energy weapon (commonly referred to as a Taser) but when that failed to have any effect, the officer pulled out his service revolver.

The incident at Gillies Lake took place on the morning of that Saturday when police officers were called the ambulance base on the ground floor of the Cochrane District Social Services Administration Board building, located at 500 Algonquin Blvd.

In a statement from SIU, "The director of the Special Investigations Unit, Tony Loparco, has determined there are no reasonable grounds to lay criminal charges against a Timmins Police Service officer in relation to the shooting death of 21-year-old Joey Knapaysweet on Feb. 3, 2018."
Knapaysweet ignored demands to drop the knife, came at the officer and the officer fired four times.

The other matter investigated by SIU involved Agnes Sutherland, 62, a member of Fort Albany First Nation, who had been placed under arrest for uttering threats but died on Sunday, Feb. 4, 2018 of "complications of end-stage diabetic nephropathy in a woman with ischemic heart disease."

She had several serious medical health issues, including kidney failure (for which she required dialysis three times per week), diabetes (which contributed to the amputation of one of her legs) and heart disease.
Two days prior to her death, she began to refuse treatment.

Loparco determined "there are no reasonable grounds to lay criminal charges against a Timmins Police Service officer in relation to the death of 62-year-old Agnes Sutherland following her interaction with police on Feb. 3, 2018."
The incidents occurred on the same weekend but were unrelated.

The SIU issued its decision on both matters on Friday. The SIU interviewed 16 civilian witnesses and three Timmins Police officers while investigating the Knapaysweet shooting incident. The notes of five other officers were reviewed as part of the investigation.

According to the SIU's summary of that incident: At 10:09 a.m. on Feb. 3, 2018, paramedics from the Cochrane District Emergency Medical Services (EMS), located at 500 Algonquin Blvd. E. in the City of Timmins, requested police assistance regarding a male (Knapaysweet) who had walked into the ambulance bay.

Prior to the arrival of the police, the Knapaysweet entered the ambulance bay and told the paramedics that he wanted someone to shoot him in the head, resulting in a second call from EMS to the TPS communications reporting that the male was hallucinating and insisting he wanted to be shot in the head.

While the paramedics were trying to communicate with the Knapaysweet, he put two knives to his throat and asked if he should do it himself. Paramedics were able to convince the him to remove the knives from his throat and calmly directed him to leave the ambulance bay. Knapaysweet complied and went out into the back parking lot located behind the ambulance base.
The first officer to arrive on the scene tried to converse with Knapaysweet (referred to in the report as the Complainant) but he lunged at the officer while holding the two knives.

The officer "immediately jumped back and retreated to the passenger side of his police vehicle while drawing his Conducted Energy Weapon (CEW) and pointing it at the Complainant. The Complainant then backed away from the police cruiser and fled the parking lot, running northbound towards Gillies Lake," the SIU stated.
The officer pursued Knapaysweet on foot. While the Complainant was running, he discarded his backpack and one of the knives.

At some point after the shooting while police were gathering evidence at the scene, officers found a "to do" list in that discarded backpack. At the top of that list Knapaysweet had written "kill every cop in town."
The initial arriving officers radioed other TPS members and alerted them that the Complainant was armed with knives and was heading in the direction of Gillies Lake.

The officer who was the subject of the investigation heard the radio transmissions and drove his police vehicle to the Gillies Conservation Area parking lot, where he saw Knapaysweet running northbound through the parking lot toward the snow-covered lake.
The subject officer exited his police vehicle and chased after Knapaysweet and out onto the frozen lake.

The subject officer drew his conducted energy weapon and pointed it at the Knapaysweet, while telling him to drop the knife, but the Knapaysweet refused to do so. The subject officer then deployed his CEW directly at Knapaysweet, but it appeared to be ineffective and the Knapaysweet advanced toward the officer, with the knife still in his hand, according to the report

The officer dropped his CEW and "transitioned to his service pistol (this is captured on the CCTV footage), firing a volley of four shots at the Complainant. The Complainant then fell forward into the snow, about two metres in front of the" officer. "The Complainant remained conscious and continued to hold onto the knife, while in a partially seated position in the snow. The (officer) continued to repeat commands to drop the knife, while he maintained gunpoint coverage of the Complainant until other police units arrived.

Two additional officers then arrived and the knife was removed from the Complainant's hand. When a third officer arrived shortly thereafter, all four police officers carried the Complainant across the lake to a waiting ambulance. The Complainant was then transported to hospital, where he was later pronounced dead at 10:45 a.m."

On Feb. 5, 2018, a post-mortem examination was performed on the Complainant's body. The attending forensic pathologist determined the cause of death as being due to multiple gunshot wounds leading to exsanguination (blood loss) and hemorrhagic shock.
